name: S&P 500 buy and hold

origin.source_title: S&P 500 index (historical annual returns compiled by Aswath Damodaran)

how_it_works.simple: Buy a little piece of the 500 biggest US companies and keep it. You get their dividends and their growth.
how_it_works.analogy: Like planting an orchard of 500 trees and never picking which ones; some die, but the orchard as a whole grows.
how_it_works.precise: A capitalization-weighted long-only position in the S&P 500 total return index, rebalanced only by the index provider. Its excess return over T-bills is the US equity risk premium. This is the benchmark parity must beat after costs and on a risk-adjusted basis.

rule: Hold 100% in an S&P 500 total return index fund (or SPY with dividends reinvested) at all times; never trade except to reinvest dividends.
data_needed: S&P 500 total return index, daily or monthly
economic_rationale: Investors demand a premium for holding risky equities rather than safe bills; Damodaran's annual data show S&P 500 returns well above T-bills since 1928.
why_it_might_fail: Long stretches of poor returns are possible: per the Damodaran data the worst calendar year since 1928 was -43.8%, and from 2000 to 2025 the index compounded about 8.0% a year versus about 10.0% over the full 1928 to 2025 span.

reported_results.source: Our calculation from Damodaran historical returns (S&P 500 incl. dividends)
reported_results.notes: Computed by the catalog from the annual return table on the page. annual_return is the geometric mean; volatility is the standard deviation of annual returns; Sharpe uses annual excess over 3-month T-bills; drawdown measured on annual data, so it understates the intra-year drawdown.
Single calendar year return printed on the page (page updated January 5, 2026).

reported_results.source: Our calculation from Kenneth French data library, US market (Mkt-RF + RF)
reported_results.notes: Computed by the catalog on 2026-10-20 from the data file at source_url; this exact figure is not printed by the source. Arithmetic mean of monthly returns times 12; volatility is monthly standard deviation times sqrt(12); Sharpe uses excess returns; max drawdown from monthly compounding. annual_return here is the compound annual total return. CRSP total market, a close proxy for the S&P 500, not the S&P 500 itself.

Arithmetic mean of monthly returns times 12; volatility is monthly standard deviation times sqrt(12); Sharpe uses excess returns; max drawdown from monthly compounding. annual_return is the compound annual total return. Window roughly matches the life of SPY (launched 1993).

post_publication_evidence: Not a published anomaly. The premium has persisted: in the Damodaran data the S&P 500 compounded about 8.0% a year over 2000 to 2025, lower than the 10.0% long-run figure but still well above T-bills (about 1.9% a year over the same span).

implementations.notes: Performance statistics (CAGR, drawdown, Sharpe) for a price series.
Backtesting framework; a buy and hold benchmark is a one-line strategy.

relevance.reason: This is the benchmark parity is trying to beat, so its return, volatility and drawdown set the bar.

research.notes: Our benchmark, run in every batch; it tests no hypothesis. Since DEC-0008 it is measured with the Fama and French US total market return extended by the S&P 500 index (daily correlation with SPY about 0.98). RUN-000001 and RUN-000002 used SPY from Yahoo.
